title: Soft-cancel button interaction and theme-sensitive loading skeletons
creator: Ava Kim
description: Introduce a 'soft-cancel' interaction pattern and theme-aware loading skeletons for button components across the design system. The soft-cancel pattern allows an actionable button to render a cancellable progress affordance when a long-running action starts (e.g., file upload, model run) while preserving immediate tap/click cancellation. Theme-sensitive skeletons ensure that loading states respect semantic tokens for light, dark, and high-contrast themes and avoid regressions introduced by previous token refactors. This ticket covers the visual spec, interaction states (idle, pressed, loading-start, loading-cancelable, loading-fixed, disabled), accessibility considerations (keyboard cancel, screen reader announcements), and handoff artifacts for engineering. Key goals: reduce layout shift during transition to spinner/skeleton, keep icon-only buttons stable (no jitter), preserve a11y semantics, and provide clear migration tokens for devs to adopt new skeleton tokens.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Soft-cancel state implemented for primary and icon-only buttons; cancel is keyboard accessible via Escape and screen-reader announced; 2) Loading skeletons use new semantic tokens and visually match Figma across light/dark/high-contrast; 3) No layout shift >4px on transition for any button size; 4) Regression tests added to design QA checklist and e2e harness; 5) PR reviewed by Design + ENG and linked in ticket
comments: 2026-02-20 Ava Kim: Created ticket after session with PM and Eng. Problem: several product flows saw sudden layout shift when switching to spinner token last quarter. Goal is to rework the state transition so it's cancelable and token-friendly.

2026-02-24 Diego Martinez: Did initial pairing with frontend on transition timing. Proposed approach: preserve inline width by reserving icon width and crossfade opacity between label and skeleton. Risks: older browsers may repaint leading to 1-frame jitter—mitigation: use will-change and transform-based opacity transitions.

2026-02-26 Priya Sharma (PM): Requested telemetry hooks so product can measure cancel rates and latency-to-cancel. Added ENG dependency for event naming (button.action.start, button.action.cancel, button.action.complete).

2026-02-28 Design review: Iterated skeleton token values to match high-contrast requirements. Agreed on two skeleton families: surface-skeleton (for compact buttons) and label-skeleton (for prominent/sized buttons). Action: update token names and spec in Confluence.

2026-03-01 Diego Martinez: Submitted initial implementation PR #1287 (WIP). Notes in PR: added unit test for keyboard escape cancellation and a regression test to verify no layout shift > 4px for the 'compact' scale. Pending: visual polish for icon-only focus ring in dark theme.

2026-03-03 Accessibility review by Maya Patel: Verified that ARIA-live announcement pattern is acceptable when button enters cancellable loading; requested change to call out 'Action started, press Escape to cancel' for screen readers. Updated copy in design spec.
2026-03-04 Ava Kim: Updated ticket with final token mapping and migration notes. Marked for design approval. Please leave final feedback on Figma by 2026-03-06.
notes: Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag, 2) Deploy to staging and run visual regression suite (Percy) and e2e cancelability scenarios, 3) Enable for 10% of Hosted API Console traffic for two days and monitor cancel metrics, layout-shift telemetry, and a11y errors, 4) Ramp to 100% if stable. Backout: revert feature flag and publish a quick patch reusing previous spinner token. Known trade-offs: reserving width for skeleton reduces fluid compression for very small text changes; chosen to favor stability over compactness. Follow-ups: create token alias deprecation RFC for older spinner tokens and schedule ENG task to propagate telemetry events to analytics.
qa_checklist: 1) Keyboard: Enter to start, Escape to cancel; 2) Screen reader reads start+cancellable copy; 3) No >4px layout shift across scales and themes; 4) Icon-only button stays visually centered during transitions; 5) Reduced motion respects user preference (fade-only no transform)
